# Introduction

(From Y Combinator Case Project)

I led the data modeling and analytics in this project to identify patterns behind successful Y Combinator startups.

Using relational schemas and SQL queries on a 1,500+ startup/founder dataset, I analyzed industry distribution, founder backgrounds, and geographic trends. Results showed that consumer tech startups, Stanford/Google founders, and US-based teams had notably higher success likelihood.

These findings helped simulate real-world accelerator selection logic and taught me how to turn messy founder data into actionable recommendations.
